title: Programa Portugal-Berkeley (Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley)
official_source: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT), with FLAD and University of California, Berkeley
duration: Research stay of up to 6 months at UC Berkeley; arrival cannot occur earlier than six months after selection
description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. title: Programa RESTART — 4ª Edição (FCT research funding after parental leave)
official_source: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT), I.P.
description: RESTART is an FCT funding instrument that competitively finances individual R&D projects in all scientific domains for researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including adoption leave. The award is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 per project for a maximum of 18 months, drawn from a total budget allocation of EUR 1.6 million, and it is held by the beneficiary R&D unit rather than paid as a personal living stipend. title: CLP Future Conservationist Awards 2027
degree: Not applicable - professional project grant, no degree awarded
official_source: Conservation Leadership Programme (BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora International and the Wildlife Conservation Society)
duration: Project duration must be between six and 12 months.
description: Annual CLP Future Conservationist Awards offer early-career conservationists a project grant of up to $15,000 as well as ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship. For 2027 the process runs in two stages: a concept note first, then a full application from shortlisted concepts only.

title: Rufford Small Grants Programme
description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. title: Whitley Awards 2027
degree: Not applicable - professional project award, no degree awarded
duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year. Winners are announced at the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
description: Awarded annually, Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders, providing funding to support and scale up proven, science-based solutions that deliver lasting impact for both people and nature. Winning a Whitley Award can be a transformative moment in a conservation leader's career, bringing international recognition, communications and media support, and entry to a global community of more than 230 conservation leaders across over 80 countries.

title: Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships 2027
description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.

title: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship (Class of 2028)
program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship with leadership development programme
duration: Maximum two years of funding; one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Masters
description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship combines financial support with a leadership programme built on the founding principles of reconciliation, education, entrepreneurship and leadership, challenging scholars to grow and connecting them to young African changemakers. It offers comprehensive funding for the core costs of a one-year Honours or two-year Masters degree at a recognised South African institution.
